sentences.zh: 吐谷渾

translations.literal: Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun

sentences.zh: =吐谷渾，慕容廆之庶長兄也，其父涉歸分部落一千七百家以隸之。

translations.literal: [Table entry:] Tuyuhun was Murong Hui's eldest brother by a concubine; his father Shegui apportioned seventeen hundred households of the tribe to be subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun was Murong Hui's senior half-brother; their father Shegui assigned him seventeen hundred families.

sentences.zh: 及涉歸卒，廆嗣位，而二部馬鬥，廆怒曰：「先公分建有別，奈何不相遠離，而令馬鬥！

translations.literal: When Shegui died, Hui succeeded to the position, but the two divisions' horses fought; Hui angrily said: 'The former lord divided the founding with distinctions—why do you not keep far apart, and instead make the horses fight!'
translations.idiomatic: After Shegui's death Murong Hui took the throne; when herds from the two camps brawled, Hui fumed: 'Our father split the herds for a reason—why mingle them until the stallions fight?'

sentences.zh: 」吐谷渾曰：「馬爲畜耳，鬥其常性，何怒於人！

translations.literal: ' Tuyuhun said: 'Horses are only beasts; fighting is their constant nature—why take anger out on men!'
translations.idiomatic: ' Tuyuhun retorted: 'Horses are animals; scrapping is what they do—why blame us?'

sentences.zh: 乖別甚易，當去汝於萬里之外矣。

translations.literal: To split apart is very easy; I ought to leave you beyond ten thousand li.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Breaking away is simple enough: I will take my people ten thousand li from you.'

sentences.zh: 」於是遂行。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he set out.
translations.idiomatic: ' With that he struck westward.

sentences.zh: 廆悔之，遣其長史史那蔞馮及父時耆舊追還之。

translations.literal: Hui regretted it and dispatched his chief clerk Shinalou Feng and the elders from his father's time to pursue and bring him back.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui thought better of it and sent chief clerk Shinalou Feng and his father's old retainers to overtake him.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾曰：「先公稱卜筮之言，當有二子克昌，祚流後裔。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun said: 'The former lord declared the divination's words—that there should be two sons who would flourish and that blessing would flow to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: ' Tuyuhun answered: 'Father's oracle promised two thriving lines whose fortune would reach distant heirs.'

sentences.zh: 我卑庶也、理無並大，今因馬而別，殆天所啟乎！

translations.literal: I am the lowborn one; by principle there is no sharing greatness; now because of horses we part—perhaps Heaven opens it!'
translations.idiomatic: ' I am the younger son with no claim to equal rank; if Heaven means us to divide over a horse fight, so be it.'

sentences.zh: 諸君試驅馬令東，馬若還東，我當相隨去矣。

translations.literal: Gentlemen, try driving the horses east; if the horses return east, I ought to follow and go.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Try driving the herds east—if they wheel west again, I will follow fate westward.'

sentences.zh: 」樓馮遣從者二千騎，擁馬東出數百步，輒悲鳴西走。

translations.literal: ' Lou Feng dispatched two thousand mounted followers, herding the horses east several hundred paces; they then whinnied mournfully and ran west.
translations.idiomatic: ' Feng sent two thousand riders to prod the herds east, but within a few hundred paces the animals wheeled west, wailing.'

sentences.zh: 如是者十餘輩，樓馮跪而言曰：「此非人事也。

translations.literal: ' Thus more than ten times; Lou Feng knelt and said: 'This is not human affair.'
translations.idiomatic: ' After a dozen attempts Feng knelt and admitted: 'This is beyond human power.'

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: ' He gave up the chase.'

sentences.zh: 鮮卑謂兄爲阿幹，廆追思之，作《阿幹之歌》，歲暮窮思，常歌之。

translations.literal: The Xianbei call an elder brother agan; Hui pursued thoughts of him and composed the 'Song of Agan'; at year's end in utter longing he often sang it.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbei calls an elder brother agan; Murong Hui composed the 'Agan Song' and sang it each year-end, brooding on his lost brother.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾謂其部落曰：「我兄弟俱當享國，廆及曾玄才百餘年耳。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun said to his tribe: 'My brothers alike ought to enjoy the state; Hui and his line will flourish only a hundred-odd years.
translations.idiomatic: ' Tuyuhun told his followers: 'Murong Hui may rule a century, no more.'

sentences.zh: 我玄孫已後，庶其昌乎！

translations.literal: After my great-grandsons, perhaps they will flourish!'
translations.idiomatic: ' From my great-grandsons onward, our line will rise.'

sentences.zh: 」於是乃西附陰山。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he attached west to the Yin Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: ' He then moved west to the Yinshan range.'

sentences.zh: 屬永嘉之亂，始度隴而西，其後子孫據有西零已西甘松之界，極乎白蘭數千里。

translations.literal: When the Yongjia turmoil came, he first crossed Long and went west; afterwards his sons and grandsons held the region from west of Xiling to the border of Gansong, reaching to Bailan for several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongjia catastrophe struck he crossed Longxi westward; later generations held the belt from west of Xiling to Gansong and onward to Bailan—several thousand li of steppe.

sentences.zh: 然有城郭而不居，隨逐水草，廬帳爲屋，以肉酪爲糧。

translations.literal: Yet they had walls and moats but did not dwell in them; they followed water and grass, took felt tents as houses, and used flesh and kumiss as grain.
translations.idiomatic: They built towns but lived in felt tents, following pasture, and lived on meat and fermented milk.

sentences.zh: 其官置長史、司馬、將軍，頗識文字。

translations.literal: Their offices set chief clerks, majors, and generals; they were somewhat literate.
translations.idiomatic: They appointed chief clerks, majors, and generals, and had a modest command of writing.

sentences.zh: 其男子通服長裙，帽或戴冪䍦。

translations.literal: Their men generally wore long skirts; on the cap some wore a face veil.
translations.idiomatic: Men wore long skirts and sometimes veiled caps.

sentences.zh: 婦人以金花爲首飾，辮髪縈後，綴以珠貝。

translations.literal: Women used gold flowers as head ornaments, braided the hair coiled behind, and strung pearls and cowries.
translations.idiomatic: Women braided their hair, coiled it behind, and decked it with gold flowers, pearls, and shell.

sentences.zh: 其婚姻，富家厚出娉財，竊女而去。

translations.literal: In their marriages, rich families lavishly put out bride wealth and steal the girl away.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy houses pay heavy bride-prices and carry off brides by elopement.

sentences.zh: 父卒，妻其群母；

translations.literal: When the father dies, the son takes his stepmothers as wives;
translations.idiomatic: When a father dies, his heir takes the widowed concubines as wives under their levirate custom.

sentences.zh: 兄亡，妻其諸嫂。

translations.literal: When the elder brother dies, the younger brother takes his sisters-in-law as wives.
translations.idiomatic: When an elder brother dies, his younger brothers marry the widows in the same fashion.

sentences.zh: 喪服制，葬訖而除。

translations.literal: Mourning garments are regulated; when burial is finished, mourning is removed.
translations.idiomatic: They observe mourning grades but shed them as soon as the burial ends.

sentences.zh: 國無常稅，調用不給，輒斂富室商人，取足而止。

translations.literal: The state had no regular taxes; when requisitions were insufficient, then they levied rich houses and merchants, taking enough and stopping.
translations.idiomatic: There was no fixed tax schedule—shortfalls were met by squeezing merchants and rich households until the need was covered.

sentences.zh: 殺人及盜馬者罪至死，他犯則征物以贖。

translations.literal: Murder and horse theft were crimes to death; other offenses were redeemed by levying goods.
translations.idiomatic: Murder and horse theft brought execution; lesser crimes were ransomed with goods.

sentences.zh: 地宜大麥，而多蔓菁，頗有菽粟。

translations.literal: The land suits great barley, and there is much turnip, and quite beans and millet.
translations.idiomatic: The soil favors barley and turnips, with some beans and millet.

sentences.zh: 出蜀馬、犛牛。

translations.literal: They produce Shu horses and yak.
translations.idiomatic: They export Sichuan-style horses and yaks.

sentences.zh: 西北雜種謂之爲阿柴虜，或號爲野虜焉。

translations.literal: Northwestern mixed peoples call them the Acha barbarians, or style them the wild barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Northwestern tribes call them the Acha Rong, or simply 'the wild Rong.'

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾年七十二卒，有子六十人，長曰吐延，嗣。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun died at age seventy-two; he had sixty sons; the eldest was Tuyan, who succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun died at seventy-two, leaving sixty sons; the eldest, Tuyan, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 吐延身長七尺八寸，雄姿魁傑，羌虜憚之，號曰項羽。

translations.literal: Tuyan's body was seven chi eight cun tall; his heroic bearing was outstanding; the Qiang and barbarians feared him and styled him Xiang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyan stood seven feet eight inches, towered like a champion, and the Qiang dubbed him their 'Xiang Yu.'

sentences.zh: 性俶儻不群，嘗慷慨謂其下曰：「大丈夫生不在中國，當高光之世，與韓、彭、吳、鄧並驅中原，定天下雌雄，使名垂竹帛，而潛竄窮山，隔在殊俗，不聞禮教於上京，不得策名於天府，生與麋鹿同群，死作氈裘之鬼，雖偷觀日月，獨不愧於心乎！

translations.literal: By nature he was unconventional and not herd-like; he once said boldly to his subordinates: 'A great man, if he is not born in China in the age of Gaozu and Guangwu, ought to ride with Han Xin, Peng Yue, Wu Qi, and Deng Yu across the Central Plain, settling who is cock and who is hen under heaven, and letting his name hang on bamboo and silk; yet skulking in exhausted mountains, cut off in alien customs, not hearing ritual teaching in the upper capital, not being able to register his name in the celestial storehouse—living in the same herd as elk and deer, dying to be a ghost in felt and fur—though he steals a view of sun and moon, is he not ashamed in his heart!'
translations.idiomatic: 'If a hero misses the Han founding age,' he told his men, 'he should still have matched Han Xin or Wu Qi on the Central Plain; hiding in barbarian hills, cut off from the capital's rites, nameless in heaven's registers, living like a deer and dying a felt-tent ghost—can such a life face the sun without shame?'

sentences.zh: 」性酷忍，而負其智，不能恤下，爲羌酋薑聰所刺。

translations.literal: ' By nature he was cruel and endured little, yet trusted his cleverness, could not pity subordinates, and was stabbed by the Qiang chief Jiang Cong.
translations.idiomatic: ' He was ruthless, arrogant, and harsh to his men, until the Qiang chief Jiang Cong assassinated him.'

sentences.zh: 劍猶在其身，謂其將紇拔泥曰：「豎子刺吾，吾之過也，上負先公，下愧士女。

translations.literal: The sword was still in his body; he said to his general Heba Ni: 'The stripling stabbed me—it is my fault; above I fail the former lord, below I shame gentlemen and ladies.
translations.idiomatic: ' With the blade still in his chest he told general Heba Ni: 'That boy skewered me through my own fault—I have failed our father and shamed my people.'

sentences.zh: 所以控制諸羌者，以吾故也。

translations.literal: The reason I controlled the various Qiang was because of me.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Only I held the Qiang in check.'

sentences.zh: 吾死之後，善相葉延，速保白蘭。

translations.literal: After I die, treat Yeyan well and quickly secure Bailan.'
translations.idiomatic: ' After my death, guard Yeyan and fall back on the Bailan fastness.'

sentences.zh: 」言終而卒。

translations.literal: ' With his words ended he died.
translations.idiomatic: ' He died as he finished speaking.'

sentences.zh: 在位十三年，有子十二人，長子葉延嗣。

translations.literal: He held position thirteen years; he had twelve sons; the eldest son Yeyan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled thirteen years and left twelve sons; Yeyan, the eldest, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 葉延年十歲，其父爲羌酋薑聰所害，每旦縛草爲薑聰之象，哭而射之，中之則號泣，不中則瞋目大呼。

translations.literal: When Yeyan was ten years old, his father was killed by the Qiang chief Jiang Cong; each morning he bound straw into the likeness of Jiang Cong, wept and shot at it; if he hit it he wailed; if he did not hit he glared and shouted greatly.
translations.idiomatic: At ten, after Jiang Cong murdered his father, Yeyan shaped straw effigies of Cong each dawn, weeping as he shot them—wailing when he hit, roaring when he missed.

sentences.zh: 其母謂曰：「姜聰，諸將已屠鱠之矣，汝何爲如此？

translations.literal: His mother said to him: 'Jiang Cong—the generals have already minced him; why are you like this?'
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, 'Jiang Cong is dead—your officers minced him already—why torture yourself?'

sentences.zh: 」葉延泣曰：「誠知射草人不益于先仇，以申罔極之志耳。

translations.literal: ' Yeyan wept saying: 'I truly know shooting straw men does not benefit the former revenge; it is only to declare the utmost of intent.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Yeyan wept, 'I know straw targets do not kill my enemy; I only vent a child's bottomless grief.'

sentences.zh: 」性至孝，母病，五日不食，葉延亦不食。

translations.literal: ' By nature he was utmost filial; when his mother fell ill, for five days he did not eat; Yeyan likewise did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: ' He was deeply filial: when his mother took ill he fasted five days, and Yeyan fasted with her.'

sentences.zh: 長而沈毅，好問天地造化、帝王年曆。

translations.literal: Growing up he was deep and resolute, fond of asking about heaven and earth's creation and transformation, and emperors' year chronologies.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he grew grave and inquisitive, pressing visitors about cosmogony and dynastic chronology.

sentences.zh: 司馬薄洛鄰曰：「臣等不學，實未審三皇何父之子，五帝誰母所生。

translations.literal: His steward Boluolin said: 'We ministers are unlearned and truly do not know of whom the Three August Ones were sons, or from which mothers the Five Emperors were born.'
translations.idiomatic: Steward Boluolin admitted, 'We are ignorant—we cannot say who fathered the Three Sovereigns or who bore the Five Emperors.'

sentences.zh: 」延曰：「自羲皇以來，符命玄象昭言著見，而卿等面牆，何其鄙哉！

translations.literal: ' Yeyan said: 'Since Fuxi, talismanic commands and dark signs have shone bright and manifest, yet you face walls—how base!'
translations.idiomatic: ' Yeyan snapped, 'Since Fuxi, heaven's omens have been plain as print—how can you plead ignorance?'

sentences.zh: 語曰『夏蟲不知冬冰』，良不虛也。

translations.literal: ' The saying goes, "Summer insects do not know winter ice"—it is truly not empty.'
translations.idiomatic: ' As the proverb says, summer bugs know nothing of winter ice—you prove it.'

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「《禮》云『公孫之子得以王父字爲氏』，吾祖始自昌黎光宅於此，今以吐谷渾爲氏，尊祖之義也。

translations.literal: ' He further said: 'The Rites states, "A ducal grandson's son may take his grandfather's style as surname"; my ancestor first from Changli radiantly dwelt here; now taking Tuyuhun as surname is the meaning of honoring the ancestor.'
translations.idiomatic: ' He added: The Rites allow a grandson to adopt a grandfather's name as clan; our forebear came out of Changli to settle here, so we will call ourselves Tuyuhun in his honor.'

sentences.zh: 」在位二十三年卒，年三十三。

translations.literal: ' He held position twenty-three years and died, age thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: ' He reigned twenty-three years and died at thirty-three.'

sentences.zh: 有子四人，長子辟奚嗣。

translations.literal: He had four sons; the eldest son Pixi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He left four sons; Pixi, the eldest, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 辟奚性仁厚慈惠。

translations.literal: Pixi by nature was benevolent, thick, kind, and gracious.
translations.idiomatic: Pixi was mild, generous, and humane.

sentences.zh: 初聞苻堅之盛，遣使獻馬五十匹，金銀五百斤。

translations.literal: When he first heard of Fu Jian's greatness, he dispatched envoys to present fifty horses and five hundred jin of gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Fu Jian's power, he sent fifty horses and five hundred jin of gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 堅大悅，拜爲安遠將軍。

translations.literal: Jian was greatly pleased and appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was delighted and named him General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 時辟奚三弟皆專恣，長史鐘惡地恐爲國害，謂司馬乞宿雲曰：「昔鄭莊公、秦昭王以一弟之寵，宗祀幾傾，況今三孽並驕，必爲社稷之患。

translations.literal: At that time Pixi's three younger brothers all acted willfully; Chief Clerk Zhong Edi feared they would harm the state and said to Major Qisuyun: 'Formerly Duke Zhuang of Zheng and King Zhaoxiang of Qin, because of one younger brother's favor, the ancestral temple nearly toppled—how much more now when three wicked ones together are arrogant—they will surely be a bane to the altars!'
translations.idiomatic: Pixi's three brothers grew overbearing; chief clerk Zhong Edi told major Qisuyun, 'Duke Zhuang of Zheng and King Zhaoxiang of Qin nearly lost the state to spoiled brothers—three such men will ruin us.'

sentences.zh: 吾與公忝當元輔，若獲保首領以沒于地，先君有問，其將何辭！

translations.literal: You and I shamefully occupy chief ministers; if we preserve our heads only to die to the ground, when the former lord asks, what words shall we have!'
translations.idiomatic: If we cling to our necks while the realm collapses, what will we say to our late lord?'

sentences.zh: 吾今誅之矣。

translations.literal: Now I shall execute them.'
translations.idiomatic: ' I mean to kill them now.'

sentences.zh: 」宿雲請白辟奚，惡地曰：「吾王無斷，不可以告。

translations.literal: ' Suyun asked leave to inform Pixi; Edi said: 'Our king lacks decision—this cannot be told.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Suyun wished to warn Pixi, but Edi said their soft king must not hear the plot.'

sentences.zh: 」於是因群下入覲，遂執三弟而誅之。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon, borrowing entry of the crowd to audience, they then seized the three younger brothers and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: ' They entered court with the crowd, seized the three royal brothers, and put them to death.'

sentences.zh: 辟奚自投於床，惡地等奔而扶之，曰：「臣昨夢先王告臣云：『三弟將爲逆亂，汝速除之。

translations.literal: Pixi threw himself on the couch; Edi and others ran and supported him, saying: 'Yesterday your servant dreamed the former lord told your servant: "The three younger brothers will commit treason and rebellion—you must speedily remove them."
translations.idiomatic: ' Pixi collapsed on his couch; Edi caught him and lied, "I dreamed your late father commanded me: the three princes mean to rebel—purge them at once."'

sentences.zh: 』臣謹奉先王之命矣。

translations.literal: ' Your servant respectfully carried out the former lord's command.'
translations.idiomatic: ' I have obeyed that ghostly order.'

sentences.zh: 」辟奚素友愛，因恍惚成疾，謂世子視連曰：「吾禍滅同生，何以見之於地下！

translations.literal: ' Pixi by nature had always loved kinship; therefore in a daze he fell ill and said to the heir apparent Shilian: 'My calamity has extinguished those born with me—how shall I see them underground!'
translations.idiomatic: ' Pixi, ever fond of his brothers, sickened with grief and told crown prince Shilian, "I have murdered my own blood—how can I face them below?"'

sentences.zh: 國事大小，汝宜攝之，吾餘年殘命，寄食而已。

translations.literal: State affairs, great and small, you ought to take them in hand; my remaining years and remnant life—only leaning on food will do.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Take the reins of every matter; I am only a living corpse waiting for porridge.'

sentences.zh: 」遂以憂卒。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: ' He died of a broken heart.'

sentences.zh: 在位二十五年，時年四十二。

translations.literal: He held position twenty-five years; at the time his age was forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He had reigned twenty-five years and died at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 有子六人，視連嗣。

translations.literal: He had six sons; Shilian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Six sons survived him; Shilian inherited the throne.

sentences.zh: 視連既立，通娉於乞伏乾歸，拜爲白蘭王。

translations.literal: Once Shilian had been established, he opened marriage relations with Qifu Gangui and was appointed King of Bailan.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian allied by marriage with Qifu Gangui of Western Qin and received the title King of Bailan.

sentences.zh: 視連幼廉慎有志性，以父憂卒，不知政事，不飲酒遊田七年矣。

translations.literal: Shilian in youth was incorrupt, cautious, and had determination of character; because his father died of grief, he did not understand governing affairs, did not drink wine or hunt fields for seven years.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Shilian was scrupulous and serious; mourning a father who had died of sorrow, he refused wine, hunts, and active rule for seven years.

sentences.zh: 鐘惡地進曰：「夫人君者，以德-{御}-世，以威齊衆，養以五味，娛以聲色。

translations.literal: Zhong Edi advanced and said: 'Now a lord of men uses virtue to steer the age and awe to align the multitude, nourishes them with the five flavors, and amuses them with sound and color.
translations.idiomatic: ' Zhong Edi urged him: a ruler must blend kindness with majesty, comfort the senses, and feed the people—four things sage-kings put first.'

sentences.zh: 此四者，聖帝明王之所先也，而公皆略之。

translations.literal: These four—sagely emperors and enlightened kings put them first—yet the duke has neglected them all.
translations.idiomatic: ' You have neglected all four.'

sentences.zh: 昔昭公儉嗇而喪，偃王仁義而亡，然則仁義所以存身，亦所以亡己。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Zhao was frugal and stingy and perished; King Yan of Xu was benevolent and righteous and perished—thus benevolence and righteousness are what preserve the body and also what destroy oneself.
translations.idiomatic: ' Duke Zhao of Lu starved on parsimony; King Yan of Xu perished on mercy—virtue alone can save or ruin a throne.'

sentences.zh: 經國者，德禮也；

translations.literal: What orders the state is virtue and ritual;
translations.idiomatic: ' Rites and virtue are the state's warp.'

sentences.zh: 濟世者，刑法也。

translations.literal: what aids the age is punishments and laws.
translations.idiomatic: ' Laws and punishments are its weft.'

sentences.zh: 二者或差，則綱維失緒。

translations.literal: If the two are in error, then the net-cords lose their threads.
translations.idiomatic: ' Lose either thread and the whole fabric unravels.'

sentences.zh: 明公奕葉重光，恩結西夏，雖仁孝發于天然，猶宜憲章周孔，不可獨追徐偃之仁，使刑德委而不建。

translations.literal: Illustrious duke, your house has piled glory generation on generation and bound the western Xia in kindness; although benevolent filial piety issues from heaven's nature, still you ought to model yourself on the Duke of Zhou and Confucius—you cannot solely pursue the benevolence of Xu Yan and let punishments and virtue both fall unestablished.
translations.idiomatic: ' Your clan shines with accumulated virtue, yet you must model the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, not the lone mercy of King Yan that left law empty.'

sentences.zh: 」視連泣曰：「先王追友于之痛，悲憤升遐，孤雖纂業，屍存而已。

translations.literal: ' Shilian wept saying: 'The former king pursued the pain of brotherly love, rose in grief and rage to ascend on high; though the orphan has inherited the enterprise, it is a corpse that survives only.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Shilian wept, "Father died of fraternal grief; I sit on the throne like a corpse."'

sentences.zh: 聲色游娛，豈所安也！

translations.literal: Sound, color, roaming, and amusement—how could these be what brings peace!'
translations.idiomatic: ' Music, women, and sport cannot heal me.'

sentences.zh: 綱維刑禮，付之將來。

translations.literal: The cords of the net—punishments and rites—entrust them to the future.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Leave law and ritual to a later reign.'

sentences.zh: 」臨終，謂其子視羆曰：「我高祖吐谷渾公常言子孫必有興者，永爲中國之西籓，慶流百世。

translations.literal: ' At the end of life he said to his son Shirong: 'My high ancestor Lord Tuyuhun often said that among descendants there must be those who rise and forever be the western bulwark of China, blessing flowing a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: ' Dying, he told Shirong, "Our ancestor swore an heir would rise as China's western shield for a hundred generations."'

sentences.zh: 吾已不及，汝亦不見，當在汝之子孫輩耳。

translations.literal: I have not reached it; you also will not see it—it ought to be in your sons' and grandsons' generation.'
translations.idiomatic: ' I shall miss that dawn; you will too—look for it in your children's age.'

sentences.zh: 」在位十五年而卒。

translations.literal: ' He held position fifteen years and died.
translations.idiomatic: ' He reigned fifteen years and died.'

sentences.zh: 有二子，長曰視羆，少曰烏紇堤。

translations.literal: He had two sons; the eldest was called Shirong, the younger Wugatidi.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons: Shirong and Wugatidi.

sentences.zh: 視羆性英果，有雄略，嘗從容謂博士金城騫苞曰：「《易》云：『動靜有常，剛柔斷矣。

translations.literal: Shirong by nature was heroic and decisive, had heroic strategy; once he leisurely said to the erudite of Jincheng, Qian Bao: 'The Changes states: "Motion and rest have their constants; by firm and soft they are decided."
translations.idiomatic: ' Shirong, bold and ambitious, once asked the scholar Qian Bao, "The Book of Changes says motion and rest each have their rule; firm and supple must be judged."'

sentences.zh: 』先王以仁宰世，不任威刑，所以剛柔靡斷，取輕鄰敵。

translations.literal: ' The former kings used benevolence to rule the world and did not employ awesome punishments; therefore firm and soft had no decision and they drew contempt from neighboring foes.
translations.idiomatic: ' Our fathers ruled with kindness, not terror, so we seemed soft and neighbors despised us.'

sentences.zh: 當仁不讓，豈宜拱默者乎！

translations.literal: When it is time for benevolence not to yield—how should one fold hands in silence!'
translations.idiomatic: ' When duty calls, a man cannot stay mute!'

sentences.zh: 今將秣馬厲兵，爭衡中國，先生以爲何如？

translations.literal: Now I intend to feed the horses and sharpen weapons to contend scales in China—what does the master think?'
translations.idiomatic: ' I mean to sharpen swords and vie for the Central Plain—your view?'

sentences.zh: 」苞曰：「大王之言，高世之略，秦隴英豪所願聞也。

translations.literal: ' Bao said: 'The great king's words are a strategy transcending the age; what heroes of Qin and Long wish to hear.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Bao answered, "That is a plan worthy of the age—every warrior of Longyou longs to hear it."'

sentences.zh: 」於是虛襟撫納，衆赴如歸。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he opened his bosom to soothe and accept them, and the multitude rushed to him as to home.
translations.idiomatic: ' He opened his court and recruits poured in like kin coming home.'

sentences.zh: 乞伏乾歸遣使拜爲使持節、都督龍涸已西諸軍事、沙州牧、白蘭王。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui dispatched envoys to appoint him Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs west of Longqi, Pastoral Commissioner of Sha Province, and King of Bailan.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui invested him as area commander west of Longqi, shepherd of Sha province, and King of Bailan.

sentences.zh: 視羆不受，謂使者曰：「自晉道不綱，奸雄競逐，劉、石虐亂，秦、燕跋扈，河南王處形勝之地，宜當糾合義兵，以懲不順，奈何私相假署，擬僭群凶！

translations.literal: Shirong did not accept and said to the envoy: 'Since the Jin way lost its cords, scheming heroes race one another; Liu and Shi ravage in disorder, Qin and Yan swagger in arrogance; the Prince of Henan occupies terrain of advantage—he ought to gather righteous troops to punish the disobedient—why privately confer titles and imitate the crowd of usurpers!'
translations.idiomatic: ' Shirong refused the patent and told the envoy that with China in chaos the Prince of Henan should rally loyal armies instead of handing out private commissions like every other warlord.'

sentences.zh: 寡人承五祖之休烈，控弦之士二萬，方欲掃氛秦隴，清彼沙涼，然後飲馬涇渭，戮問鼎之豎，以一丸尼封東關，閉燕趙之路，迎天子于西京，以盡遐籓之節，終不能如季孟、子陽妄自尊大。

translations.literal: The orphan inherits the splendid martial merit of five ancestors and commands twenty thousand bowmen; I am about to sweep the murk from Qin and Long, clear those Sha and Liang, then water horses in the Jing and Wei and execute the striplings who would 'ask after the tripods'—with one pellet I could choke the eastern passes, block the roads of Yan and Zhao, and welcome the Son of Heaven in the western capital, thereby exhausting the duty of a distant vassal—yet in the end I cannot be like Gongshu Shu or Li Yi in vain arrogating greatness.'
translations.idiomatic: ' I command twenty thousand riders under five heroic forebears; I will purge Qin-Liang, clear the western sands, wash my horses in the Jing and Wei, cut down pretenders who eye the tripods, seal the passes to Yan and Zhao, and escort the emperor home to Chang'an—yet I will not ape Gongshu Shu or Li Yi in crowning myself.'

sentences.zh: 爲吾白河南王，何不立勳帝室，策名王府，建當年之功，流芳來葉邪！

translations.literal: For me inform the Prince of Henan—why does he not raise merit for the imperial house, inscribe his name in the kingly register, build merit for the present age, and spread fragrance to later leaves!'
translations.idiomatic: ' Tell Gangui to serve the Jin house, earn a place in its registers, and win fame for his heirs instead.'

sentences.zh: 」乾歸大怒，然憚其強，初猶結好，後竟遣衆擊之。

translations.literal: ' Gangui was greatly angry, yet feared his strength; at first he still forged friendship, but in the end he dispatched hosts to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: ' Gangui raged yet dreaded him, feigned friendship, then sent an army.'

sentences.zh: 視羆大敗，退保白蘭。

translations.literal: Shirong was greatly defeated and withdrew to defend Bailan.
translations.idiomatic: Shirong was routed and fled to the Bailan fastness.

sentences.zh: 在位十一年，年三十三卒。

translations.literal: He held position eleven years; at age thirty-three he died.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled eleven years and died at thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 子樹洛幹年少，傳位於烏紇堤。

translations.literal: The son Shuluogan was young; the position was passed to Wugatidi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shuluogan was a minor, so the throne passed to uncle Wugatidi.

sentences.zh: 烏紇堤一名大孩，性軟弱，耽酒淫色，不恤國事。

translations.literal: Wugatidi, alternate name Dahai, by nature was soft and weak, addicted to wine and lewd with women, and did not pity state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wugatidi, also called Dahai, was a drunk and a lecher who ignored government.

sentences.zh: 乞伏乾歸之入長安也，烏紇堤屢抄其境。

translations.literal: When Qifu Gangui entered Chang'an, Wugatidi repeatedly raided his borders.
translations.idiomatic: When Gangui marched on Chang'an, Wugatidi raided his marches again and again.

sentences.zh: 乾歸怒，率騎討之。

translations.literal: Gangui was angry and led cavalry to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui struck back with a cavalry expedition.

sentences.zh: 烏紇堤大敗，亡失萬餘口，保于南涼，遂卒于胡國。

translations.literal: Wugatidi was greatly defeated, lost more than ten thousand persons, took refuge with Southern Liang, and thereupon died in the Hu state.
translations.idiomatic: Wugatidi lost ten thousand followers, fled to Southern Liang, and died among the Hu.

sentences.zh: 在位八年，時年三十五。

translations.literal: He held position eight years; at the time his age was thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned eight years and died at thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 視羆之子樹洛幹立。

translations.literal: Shirong's son Shuluogan was established.
translations.idiomatic: Shuluogan, Shirong's son, took the throne.

sentences.zh: 樹洛幹九歲而孤，其母念氏聰惠有姿色，烏紇堤妻之，有寵，遂專國事。

translations.literal: Shuluogan at nine sui was orphaned; his mother Lady Nian was clever and comely in looks; Wugatidi married her, won favor, and thereupon monopolized state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at nine, he saw his clever mother wed Wugatidi, who favored her and seized the government.

sentences.zh: 洛幹十歲便自稱世子，年十六嗣立，率所部數千家奔歸莫何川，自稱大都督、車騎大將軍、大單于、吐谷渾王。

translations.literal: At ten sui Luo Gan himself styled himself heir apparent; at sixteen sui he succeeded, led several thousand households of his division fleeing to return to the Mohe River, and styled himself grand area commander, chariot-and-cavalry great general, great shanyu, and King of Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he declared himself crown prince; at sixteen he led thousands of families to the Mohe River, proclaiming himself shanyu and King of Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 化行所部，衆庶樂業，號爲戊寅可汗，沙漒雜種莫不歸附。

translations.literal: His transforming influence spread through his following; the multitude found joy in their work and were styled the Wuyin Qaghan; mixed kinds along the sands none failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: His rule won the people; tribes hailed him as the Wuyin Qaghan and flocked to his banner.

sentences.zh: 乃宣言曰：「孤先祖避地於此，暨孤七世，思與群賢共康休緒。

translations.literal: He then proclaimed: 'The orphan's ancestors fled to dwell here; down to the orphan seven generations—We wish with all worthy men jointly to secure good fortune.'
translations.idiomatic: ' He told his nobles, "Seven generations have camped in this refuge; I want you to help me build a lasting peace."'

sentences.zh: 今士馬桓桓，控弦數萬，孤將振威梁益，稱霸西戎，觀兵三秦，遠朝天子，諸君以爲何如？

translations.literal: Now soldiers and horses are arrayed, bowmen number in the tens of thousands; the orphan will raise might in Liang and Yi, hegemonize the western Rong, display arms in the three Qin, and pay court to the Son of Heaven from afar—what do gentlemen think?'
translations.idiomatic: ' Our host counts tens of thousands—I mean to awe Liang and Yi, dominate the western tribes, show force in Sanqin, and bow to the Jin emperor—what say you?'

sentences.zh: 」衆咸曰：「此盛德之事也，願大王自勉！

translations.literal: ' The crowd all said: 'This is an affair of abundant virtue; we wish the great king to exert himself!'
translations.idiomatic: ' They cried, "That is the deed of a sage-king—lead on!"'

sentences.zh: 」乞伏乾歸甚忌之，率騎二萬，攻之於赤水。

translations.literal: ' Qifu Gangui greatly feared him and led twenty thousand cavalry to attack him at Chishui.
translations.idiomatic: ' Gangui, alarmed, brought twenty thousand riders to Chishui.'

sentences.zh: 樹洛幹大敗，遂降乾歸，乾歸拜爲平狄將軍、赤水都護，又以其弟吐護真爲捕虜將軍、層城都尉。

translations.literal: Shuluogan was greatly defeated, thereupon submitted to Gangui; Gangui appointed him General Who Pacifies the Di and Colonel Who Protects Chishui, and also made his younger brother Tuhuzhen General Who Captures Prisoners and colonel of the tiered citadel.
translations.idiomatic: Shuluogan surrendered and Gangui named him Pacifier of the Di and warden of Chishui, while his brother became warden of the frontier forts.

sentences.zh: 其後屢爲乞伏熾磐所破，又保白蘭，慚憤發病而卒。

translations.literal: Afterwards he was repeatedly broken by Qifu Chipan and again defended Bailan; shamed and angry, he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipan broke him repeatedly; he died of shame in Bailan.

sentences.zh: 在位九年，時年二十四。

translations.literal: He held position nine years; at the time his age was twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He reigned nine years and died at twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 熾磐聞其死，喜曰：「此虜矯矯，所謂有豕白蹄也。

translations.literal: When Chipan heard of his death, he rejoiced and said: 'This captive is so proud—what they call a pig with white hoofs.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Chipan sneered, "That stiff-necked barbarian is the white-hoofed pig of the omen."'

sentences.zh: 」有子四人，世子拾虔嗣。

translations.literal: ' He had four sons; the heir apparent Shiqian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: ' Four sons survived; Shiqian inherited.'

sentences.zh: 其後世嗣不絕。

translations.literal: Afterwards generations of heirs did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The line continued without break.

translations.literal: The line is an equals sign used as a table marker in the transmitted layout.
translations.idiomatic: — (source table divider)

sentences.zh: 焉耆國

translations.literal: The state of Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi (Karashahr)

sentences.zh: =焉耆國西去洛陽八千二百里，其地南至尉犁，北與烏孫接，方四百里。

translations.literal: [Table entry:] The state of Yanqi is eight thousand two hundred li west of Luoyang; its land reaches south to Yuli, north joins Wusun, and is four hundred li square.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi lies 8,200 li west of Luoyang, borders Wusun on the north and Yuli on the south, and covers some four hundred square li.

sentences.zh: 四面有大山，道險隘，百人守之，千人不過。

translations.literal: On four sides are great mountains; the roads are perilous and narrow—a hundred men guarding them, a thousand cannot pass.
translations.idiomatic: Ringed by mountains, its defiles let a hundred hold off a thousand.

sentences.zh: 其俗丈夫翦發，婦人衣襦，著大袴。

translations.literal: Their custom: husbands clip hair; women wear jackets and put on large trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Men crop their hair; women wear jackets and baggy trousers.

sentences.zh: 婚姻同華夏。

translations.literal: Marriage is like Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: Wedding rites resemble Chinese practice.

sentences.zh: 好貨利，任奸詭。

translations.literal: They love profit in goods and trust in deceit.
translations.idiomatic: They are greedy and fond of guile.

sentences.zh: 王有侍衛數十人，皆倨慢無尊卑之禮。

translations.literal: The king has several tens of guards; all are arrogant and lack ritual of high and low.
translations.idiomatic: The king keeps a few dozen guards who slouch without court etiquette.

sentences.zh: 武帝太康中，其王龍安遣子入侍。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's Taikang period, their king Long'an dispatched a son to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu, King Long'an sent a son as hostage.

sentences.zh: 安夫人獪胡之女，妊身十二月，剖脅生子，曰會，立之爲世子。

translations.literal: An's wife was a cunning Hu woman; she was pregnant twelve months, split her flank and bore a son named Hui, established him as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Long'an's Hu wife carried twelve months, bore a son named Hui from a side cut, and had him named heir.

sentences.zh: 會少而勇傑，安病篤，謂會曰：「我嘗爲龜茲王白山所辱，不忘於心。

translations.literal: Hui in youth was brave and outstanding; when An was gravely ill, he said to Hui: 'I was once shamed by the King of Kucha, Baishan; I have not forgotten it in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: The brave youth Hui heard his dying father say, "Kucha's King Baishan shamed me—never forget."'

sentences.zh: 汝能雪之，乃吾子也。

translations.literal: If you can wipe away that shame, then you are my son.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Avenge that insult and you are truly my son.'

sentences.zh: 」及會立，襲滅白山，遂據其國，遣子熙歸本國爲王。

translations.literal: ' When Hui was established, he raided and destroyed Baishan, thereupon occupied that state, and dispatched his son Xi to return to the native state as king.
translations.idiomatic: ' Hui then crushed Baishan, seized Kucha, and installed his son Xi as king of Yanqi.'

sentences.zh: 會有膽氣籌略，遂霸西胡，蔥嶺以東莫不服。

translations.literal: Hui had courage, breath, and stratagem; thereupon he hegemonized the western Hu; east of the Congling none failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Hui dominated the western regions; every state east of the Pamirs bowed.

sentences.zh: 然恃勇輕率，嘗出宿於外，爲龜茲國人羅雲所殺。

translations.literal: Yet relying on bravery he was rash; once he lodged outside on campaign and was killed by the Kucha man Luoyun.
translations.idiomatic: His rash courage killed him: a Kuchean named Luoyun murdered him on a night camp.

sentences.zh: 其後張駿遣沙州刺史楊宣率衆疆理西域，宣以部將張植爲前鋒，所向風靡。

translations.literal: Afterwards Zhang Jun dispatched the governor of Sha Province, Yang Xuan, to lead a host to extend order in the Western Regions; Xuan made his subordinate general Zhang Zhi the vanguard, and wherever he aimed the wind laid low.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Jun sent Yang Xuan west; Zhang Zhi led his van and swept all before him.

sentences.zh: 軍次其國，熙距戰於賁侖城，爲植所敗。

translations.literal: The army halted at their state; Xi resisted battle at the city of Benlun and was defeated by Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi met Zhang Zhi at Benlun and was routed.

sentences.zh: 植時屯鐵門，未至十餘-{里}-，熙又率衆先要之于遮留穀。

translations.literal: Zhi at the time was stationed at the Iron Gate; not yet having reached more than ten li, Xi again led a host first to await him in the Zhelu Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi camped at the Iron Gate; Xi ambushed him in Zhelu Gorge ten li short.

sentences.zh: 植將至，或曰：「漢祖畏于柏人，岑彭死于彭亡，今穀名遮留，殆將有伏？

translations.literal: When Zhi was about to arrive, someone said: 'Han Gaozu feared at Bairen; Cen Peng died at Pengwang—now the gorge is named Zhelu—perhaps there will be an ambush?'
translations.idiomatic: ' A soldier warned, "Emperors feared place-names—this gorge means 'detain'—expect a trap."'

sentences.zh: 」植單騎嘗之，果有伏發。

translations.literal: ' Zhi rode alone to try it, and indeed an ambush sprang.
translations.idiomatic: ' Zhi scouted alone and sprung the ambush.'

sentences.zh: 植馳擊敗之，進據尉犁，熙率群下四萬人肉袒降于宣。

translations.literal: Zhi galloped, struck, and defeated them, advanced and occupied Yuli; Xi led his subordinates forty thousand persons, bare-chested, to surrender to Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi charged through, took Yuli, and Xi surrendered forty thousand men to Yang Xuan.

sentences.zh: 呂光討西域，復降於光。

translations.literal: When Lü Guang campaigned in the Western Regions, he again submitted to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted to Lü Guang's expedition.

sentences.zh: 及光僭位，熙又遣子入侍。

translations.literal: When Guang usurped the throne, Xi again dispatched a son to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Guang seized the throne, Xi again sent a hostage.

sentences.zh: 龜茲國

translations.literal: The state of Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha

sentences.zh: =龜茲國西去洛陽八千二百八十-{里}-，俗有城郭，其城三重，中有佛塔廟千所。

translations.literal: [Table entry:] The state of Kucha is eight thousand two hundred eighty li west of Luoyang; by custom it has walls and moats; its city has three rings, and within are over a thousand Buddhist stupas and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha lies 8,280 li west of Luoyang, ringed by triple walls and a thousand Buddhist shrines.

sentences.zh: 人以田種畜牧爲業，男女皆翦發垂項。

translations.literal: People take field planting and herding as their occupation; men and women all clip hair so it hangs at the neck.
translations.idiomatic: The people farm and herd; both sexes crop their hair to neck length.

sentences.zh: 王宮壯麗，煥若神居。

translations.literal: The royal palace is magnificent, radiant as a spirit's dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The royal palace gleams like a celestial mansion.

sentences.zh: 武帝太康中，其王遣子入侍。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's Taikang period, their king dispatched a son to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu the king of Kucha sent a prince to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 惠懷末，以中國亂，遣使貢方物于張重華。

translations.literal: At the end of Hui and Huai, because China was in chaos, they dispatched envoys to present local products to Zhang Chonghua.
translations.idiomatic: As Jin collapsed at the end of Hui and Huai, they sent tribute to Zhang Chonghua of Former Liang.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時，堅遣其將呂光率衆七萬伐之，其王白純距境不降，光進軍討平之。

translations.literal: In Fu Jian's time, Jian dispatched his general Lü Guang leading seventy thousand hosts to attack them; their king Baichun barred the border and would not submit; Guang advanced the army and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian ordered Lü Guang west with seventy thousand men; King Baichun resisted until Guang crushed the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 大宛國

translations.literal: The state of Dayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dayuan (Ferghana)

sentences.zh: =大宛國去洛陽萬三千三百五十-{里}-，南至大月氏，北接康居，大小七十餘城。

translations.literal: [Table entry:] The state of Dayuan is thirteen thousand three hundred fifty li from Luoyang; south it reaches Great Yuezhi, north joins Kangju, and there are more than seventy cities large and small.
translations.idiomatic: Dayuan sits 13,350 li from Luoyang, reaches the Yuezhi on the south and Kangju on the north, and holds seventy-odd cities.

sentences.zh: 土宜稻麥，有蒲陶酒，多善馬，馬汗血。

translations.literal: The soil suits rice and wheat; there is grape wine; there are many fine horses whose horses sweat blood.
translations.idiomatic: The land grows rice and wheat, makes wine from grapes, and breeds the blood-sweating horses of legend.

sentences.zh: 其人皆深目多須。

translations.literal: Its people all have deep eyes and many beards.
translations.idiomatic: The people are deep-eyed and bearded.

sentences.zh: 其俗娶婦先以金同心指鐶爲娉，又以三婢試之。

translations.literal: Their custom in taking a wife is first to use a gold concentric finger-ring as bride wealth, and also to test her with three maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: Grooms send a gold joint ring as bride-price and test brides with three servant girls.

sentences.zh: 不男者絕婚。

translations.literal: If he is not male, the marriage is broken off.
translations.idiomatic: If the groom proves impotent, the match is voided.

sentences.zh: 姦淫有子，皆卑其母。

translations.literal: If there is fornication that produces a child, all disdain the mother.
translations.idiomatic: Children of adultery are raised to despise their mothers.

sentences.zh: 與人馬乘不調墜死者，馬主出斂具。

translations.literal: If someone falls dead from a horse ride that was not well adjusted, the horse owner supplies the funeral goods.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest falls from a poorly trained mount and dies, the horse's owner pays for the burial.

sentences.zh: 善市賈，爭分銖之利，得中國金銀，輒爲器物，不用爲幣也。

translations.literal: They are skilled at marketing and haggle over the profit of a cash-weight; when they obtain Chinese gold and silver, they always make vessels and do not use them as coin.
translations.idiomatic: They love haggling; Chinese gold and silver are cast into vessels, never left as bullion.

sentences.zh: ，武帝遣使楊顥拜其王藍庾爲大宛王。

translations.literal: (Continuing,) Emperor Wu dispatched envoy Yang Hao to invest their king Lanyu as King of Dayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu later sent Yang Hao to recognize King Lanyu of Dayuan.

sentences.zh: 藍庾卒，其子摩之立，遣使貢汗血馬，

translations.literal: When Lanyu died, his son Mozhi was established and dispatched envoys to present blood-sweating horses,
translations.idiomatic: Lanyu's son Mozhi succeeded him and sent the famous sweat-blooded horses as tribute.

translations.idiomatic: — (source table divider)

sentences.zh: 康居國

translations.literal: The state of Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: Kangju

sentences.zh: =康居國在大宛西北可二千里，與粟弋、伊列鄰接。

translations.literal: [Table entry:] The state of Kangju is about two thousand li northwest of Dayuan, adjoining Suyi and Yilie.
translations.idiomatic: Kangju lies two thousand li northwest of Ferghana, beside Suyi and Yilie.

sentences.zh: 其王居蘇薤城。

translations.literal: Their king dwells at the city of Suoxie.
translations.idiomatic: The king resides at Suoxie.

sentences.zh: 風俗及人貌、衣服略同大宛。

translations.literal: Customs and people's looks and clothes are broadly the same as Dayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dress and faces resemble Dayuan.

sentences.zh: 地和暖，饒桐柳蒲陶，多牛羊，出好馬。

translations.literal: The land is mild and warm, rich in paulownia, willows, and grapes; many oxen and sheep; it produces fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is mild, paulownia and grapes abound, herds thrive, and the horses are excellent.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，其王那鼻遣使上封事，並獻善馬。

translations.literal: In the Taishi period, their king Nabi dispatched envoys to submit a sealed memorial and also present fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi, King Nabi sent a memorial and fine horses.

translations.idiomatic: — (source table divider)

sentences.zh: 大秦國

translations.literal: The state of Da Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Da Qin (Rome)

sentences.zh: =大秦國一名犁鞬，在西海之西，其地東西南北各數千里。

translations.literal: [Table entry:] The state of Da Qin, alternate name Lijian, is west of the western sea; its land extends several thousand li in each direction.
translations.idiomatic: Da Qin—called Lijian—lies beyond the western sea, a realm thousands of li on a side.

sentences.zh: 有城邑，其城周回百餘-{里}-。

translations.literal: It has walled towns; its capital's wall runs more than a hundred li around.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital's walls stretch over a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 屋宇皆以珊瑚爲棁栭，琉璃爲牆壁，水精爲柱礎。

translations.literal: Roof beams are all of coral, eaves and lintels of colored glass, and column bases of rock crystal.
translations.idiomatic: Beams are coral, walls glass, and column bases crystal.

sentences.zh: 其王有五宮，其宮相去各十-{里}-，每旦于一宮聽事，終而復始。

translations.literal: Their king has five palaces; each palace is ten li apart from the others; each dawn he hears business in one palace and rotates through them.
translations.idiomatic: The king rotates among five palaces ten li apart, holding court in each by turns.

sentences.zh: 若國有災異，輒更立賢人，放其舊王，被放者亦不敢怨。

translations.literal: If the state has calamity or prodigy, then they replace the ruler with a worthy man and banish the old king; the banished one dares not resent.
translations.idiomatic: Disasters trigger abdication: a worthy replaces the king, who leaves without protest.

sentences.zh: 有官曹簿領，而文字習胡，亦有白蓋小車、旌旗之屬，及郵驛制置，一如中州。

translations.literal: They have bureaus, registers, and clerks, yet writing follows Hu forms; they also have small white-canopied carts, banners and flags, and post-stations arranged like the central provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaucracy, post roads, and Hu-style script mirror China.

sentences.zh: 其人長大，貌類中國人而胡服。

translations.literal: Their people are tall and large; in looks they resemble Chinese but wear Hu clothing.
translations.idiomatic: They look like Chinese giants in foreign dress.

sentences.zh: 其土多出金玉寶物、明珠、大貝，有夜光璧、駭雞犀及火浣布，又能刺金縷繡及積錦縷罽。

translations.literal: Their soil produces much gold, jade, treasures, bright pearls, and great cowries; there are night-shining disks, rhinoceros horn that frightens fowl, and fire-washed cloth; they can also embroider gold thread and pile brocade felts.
translations.idiomatic: Exports include luminous jade, fireproof cloth, and gold-thread embroidery.

sentences.zh: 以金銀爲錢，銀錢十當金錢之一。

translations.literal: They use gold and silver as coin; ten silver coins equal one gold coin.
translations.idiomatic: Silver coins trade at ten to one against gold.

sentences.zh: 安息、天竺人與之交市於海中，其利百倍。

translations.literal: People of Anxi and Tianzhu trade with them on the sea; the profit is a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: Parthian and Indian merchants reap hundredfold profits at sea.

sentences.zh: 鄰國使到者，輒廩以金錢。

translations.literal: When neighboring states' envoys arrive, they are always granaried with gold coin.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys are feasted and paid in gold.

sentences.zh: 途經大海，海水鹹苦不可食，商客往來皆齎三歲糧，是以至者稀少。

translations.literal: The route crosses a great sea; the sea water is salty and bitter and undrinkable; merchants going and coming all carry three years' grain, therefore those who arrive are few.
translations.idiomatic: The ocean crossing is so long and the water undrinkable that caravans pack three years' food, so few arrive.

sentences.zh: 漢時都護班超遣掾甘英使其國，入海，船人曰：「海中有思慕之物，往者莫不悲懷。

translations.literal: In Han times the protector-general Ban Chao dispatched clerk Gan Ying to his state; entering the sea, the boatmen said: 'In the sea there are things that stir longing; those who go none fail to feel grief and yearning.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Chao sent Gan Ying toward Rome; sailors warned of sea spirits that break the heart.'

sentences.zh: 若漢使不戀父母妻子者，可入。

translations.literal: If Han envoys do not long for parents, wives, and children, they may enter.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Only men without family ties may sail on.'

sentences.zh: 」英不能渡。

translations.literal: ' Ying could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ying turned back.

sentences.zh: 武帝太康中，其王遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's Taikang period, their king dispatched envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu the king of Da Qin sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 南蠻

translations.literal: Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Man tribes

sentences.zh: 南蠻，林邑、扶南。

translations.literal: Among the Southern Man—Linyi and Funan.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Man section covers Linyi and Funan.

translations.literal: The line is an equals sign used as a table marker in the transmitted layout.
translations.idiomatic: — (source table divider)

sentences.zh: 林邑

translations.literal: Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi (Champa)

sentences.zh: =林邑國本漢時象林縣，則馬援鑄柱之處也，去南海三千里。

translations.literal: [Table entry:] The state of Linyi was originally Xianglin County in Han times—the place where Ma Yuan cast his bronze pillar—and is three thousand li from the South Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi began as Han's Xianglin county, where Ma Yuan raised his column, three thousand li from the southern coast.

sentences.zh: 後漢末，縣功曹姓區，有子曰連，殺令自立爲王，子孫相承。

translations.literal: At the end of Later Han, the county merit officer surnamed Ou had a son named Lian who killed the magistrate and established himself as king; sons and grandsons succeeded one another.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Later Han a clerk surnamed Ou had a son Lian who murdered the magistrate and founded a royal line.

sentences.zh: 其後王無嗣，外孫范熊代立。

translations.literal: Afterwards the king had no heir; his maternal grandson Fan Xiong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When the line failed, grandson Fan Xiong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 熊死，子逸立。

translations.literal: When Xiong died, his son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xiong's son Yi followed.

sentences.zh: 其俗皆開北戶以向日，至於居止，或東西無定。

translations.literal: Their custom is all to open northern windows toward the sun; as for dwelling, sometimes east sometimes west without fixity.
translations.idiomatic: Houses face north for light; settlements shift with the seasons.

sentences.zh: 人性凶悍，果於戰鬥，便山習水，不閑平地。

translations.literal: Human nature is fierce and hardy, decisive in battle, skilled in mountains and water, unused to level ground.
translations.idiomatic: They are fierce fighters in jungle and river, awkward on open plains.

sentences.zh: 四時暄暖，無霜無雪，人皆倮露徒跣，以黑色爲美。

translations.literal: The four seasons are warm; there is no frost or snow; people all go naked and barefoot and take black color as beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Warm year-round, they go barefoot and prize dark skin.

sentences.zh: 貴女賤男，同姓爲婚，婦先娉婿。

translations.literal: They esteem women and despise men; they marry within the same surname; the woman first betroths the husband.
translations.idiomatic: Women choose husbands, same-surname marriage is allowed, and daughters rank above sons.

sentences.zh: 女嫁之時，著迦盤衣，橫幅合縫如井欄，首戴寶花。

translations.literal: When a girl marries, she wears a kapan robe, horizontal cloth sewn like a well-crib, and on the head wears jeweled flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Brides don wraparound kapan robes and jeweled crowns.

sentences.zh: 居喪翦鬢謂之孝，燔屍中野謂之葬。

translations.literal: In mourning they clip the temples and call it filial; they burn corpses in the wild and call it burial.
translations.idiomatic: They shave temples for mourning and cremate the dead in the fields.

sentences.zh: 其王服天冠，被纓絡，每聽政，子弟侍臣皆不得近之。

translations.literal: Their king wears a heaven crown and draped bead nets; whenever he hears cases, sons and younger brothers and attendant ministers may not approach near.
translations.idiomatic: The king hears lawsuits alone in heaven crown and jeweled veil.

sentences.zh: 自孫權以來，不朝中國。

translations.literal: From Sun Quan onward they did not court China.
translations.idiomatic: Since Sun Quan's day they ignored Chinese suzerainty.

sentences.zh: 至武帝太康中，始來貢獻。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu's Taikang period, they first came with tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: They first sent tribute under Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: ，範逸死，奴文纂位。

translations.literal: (Continuing,) when Fan Yi died, the slave Wen usurped the position.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yi died childless, his retainer Wen seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 文，日南西卷縣夷帥範椎奴也。

translations.literal: Wen was a slave of the Yi chieftain Fan Chui of Xijuan county in Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen had been a slave of the Fan clan head in Rinan's Xijuan.

sentences.zh: 嘗牧牛澗中，獲二鯉魚，化成鐵，用以爲刀。

translations.literal: Once he was herding oxen in a stream and caught two carp; they transformed into iron, which he used to make a knife.
translations.idiomatic: Herding cattle, he netted two carp that turned to iron and forged a blade.

sentences.zh: 刀成，乃對大石嶂而咒之曰：「鯉魚變化，冶成雙刀，石嶂破者，是有神靈。

translations.literal: When the knife was finished, then facing a great stone cliff he cursed it saying: 'Carp transformed, smelted into paired knives—if the stone cliff breaks, then there is spiritual power.
translations.idiomatic: He forged twin blades and swore at a cliff: if the rock splits, the gods favor him.'

sentences.zh: 」進斫之，石即瓦解。

translations.literal: ' He advanced and chopped it; the stone immediately crumbled.
translations.idiomatic: ' He struck and the cliff shattered.'

sentences.zh: 文知其神，乃懷之。

translations.literal: Wen knew it was divine and therefore treasured the blades.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the magical swords.

sentences.zh: 隨商賈往來，見上國制度，至林邑，遂教逸作宮室、城邑及器械。

translations.literal: Following merchants back and forth, he saw the institutions of the upper state; arriving at Linyi, he then taught Yi to build palaces, walled towns, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling with merchants he studied Chinese ways, then built Fan Yi palaces, walls, and arms.

sentences.zh: 逸甚愛信之，使爲將。

translations.literal: Yi greatly loved and trusted him and made him a general.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yi made him a favorite general.

sentences.zh: 文乃譖逸諸子，或徙或奔。

translations.literal: Wen then slandered Yi's sons; some were banished, some fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wen slandered the princes until they fled or were exiled.

sentences.zh: 及逸死，無嗣，文遂自立爲王。

translations.literal: When Yi died without heir, Wen thereupon established himself as king.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died heirless, Wen crowned himself.

sentences.zh: 以逸妻妾悉置之高樓，從己者納之，不從者絕其食。

translations.literal: He placed all of Yi's wives and concubines on a high tower; those who followed him he took in; those who did not follow he cut off food.
translations.idiomatic: He starved Fan Yi's harem on a tower, admitting only women who submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 於是乃攻大岐界、小岐界、式僕、徐狼、屈都、乾魯、扶單等諸國，並之，有衆四五萬人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he attacked the states of Great Qijie, Small Qijie, Shipu, Xulang, Qudu, Ganlu, Fudan, and others, annexed them, and had a following of forty or fifty thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: He conquered a ring of chiefdoms and gathered forty or fifty thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 遣使通表入貢於帝，其書皆胡字。

translations.literal: He dispatched envoys to present memorials and enter tribute to the emperor; their documents were all in Hu script.
translations.idiomatic: He sent memorials in Cham script and offered tribute to Jin.

sentences.zh: 至，文率其衆攻陷日南，害太守夏侯覽，殺五六千人，餘奔九真，以覽屍祭天，鏟平西卷縣城，遂據日南。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Wen led his host to attack and capture Rinan, killed Grand Warden Xia Houlan of Rinan, killed five or six thousand persons; the rest fled to Jiuzhen; he used Lan's corpse to sacrifice to heaven, leveled the walls of Xijuan county, and thereupon occupied Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen stormed Rinan, slew Warden Xia Houlan, massacred thousands, chased survivors to Jiuzhen, sacrificed the warden's body, razed Xijuan, and seized the commandery.

sentences.zh: 告交州刺史硃蕃，求以日南北鄙橫山爲界。

translations.literal: He informed the Inspector of Jiaozhou, Zhu Fan, requesting to take the northern fringe of Rinan at Mount Heng as the border.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded Mount Heng as the new frontier in a letter to Inspector Zhu Fan.

sentences.zh: 初，徼外諸國嘗齎寶物自海路來貿貨，而交州刺史、日南太守多貪利侵侮，十折二三。

translations.literal: At first, the various states beyond the pale often carried treasure goods and came by sea route to trade, but the Inspector of Jiaozhou and Grand Warden of Rinan mostly coveted profit, encroached and insulted them, taking ten or twenty or thirty percent off.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier traders had long been fleeced by greedy Jiaozhou and Rinan officials who skimmed two or three tenths of every cargo.

sentences.zh: 至刺史姜壯時，使韓戢領日南太守，戢估較太半，又伐船調枹，聲云征伐，由是諸國恚憤。

translations.literal: When it reached Inspector Jiang Zhuang, he made Han Ji hold the post of Grand Warden of Rinan; Ji assessed levies at more than half, again requisitioned boats and oars, claiming aloud a campaign—therefore the various states resented and raged.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiang Zhuang, Han Ji as warden seized more than half their goods and pressed boats for a phantom war, enraging every kingdom.

sentences.zh: 且林邑少田，貪日南之地，戢死絕，繼以謝擢，侵刻如初。

translations.literal: Moreover Linyi had little farmland and coveted Rinan's land; when Ji died the thread snapped, and Xie Zhuo succeeded, encroaching as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi lacked fields and coveted Rinan; when Han Ji died, Xie Zhuo resumed the extortion.

sentences.zh: 及覽至郡，又耽荒於酒，政教愈亂，故被破滅。

translations.literal: When Lan reached the commandery, again he wallowed in wine; government and teaching grew ever more chaotic; therefore they were broken and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Warden Lan drank away his administration, so the coast fell to Wen.

sentences.zh: 既而文還林邑。

translations.literal: Afterwards Wen returned to Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wen then withdrew to Linyi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，硃蕃使督護劉雄戍于日南，文復攻陷之。

translations.literal: That year Zhu Fan sent Area Commander Liu Xiong to garrison Rinan; Wen again attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fan sent Liu Xiong to recover Rinan; Wen crushed him too.

sentences.zh: 四年，文又襲九真，害士庶十八九。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Wen again raided Jiuzhen, killing eighteen or nineteen tenths of gentlemen and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he ravaged Jiuzhen and slaughtered nine in ten of the people.

sentences.zh: 明年，征西督護滕畯率交廣之兵伐文于盧容，爲文所敗，退次九真。

translations.literal: The next year, the western expedition Area Commander Teng Jun led the troops of Jiao and Guang to attack Wen at Lurong and was defeated by Wen; he withdrew to halt at Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Teng Jun attacked him at Lurong and was routed, falling back to Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 其年，文死，子佛嗣。

translations.literal: That year Wen died; his son Fo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Wen died and his son Fo inherited.

sentences.zh: 升平末，廣州刺史勝含率衆伐之，佛懼，請降，含與盟而還。

translations.literal: At the end of Shengping, Inspector of Guangzhou Sheng Han led a host to attack him; Fo feared, begged to submit; Han made covenant with him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Shengping's end Sheng Han forced Fo to surrender and withdrew after a treaty.

sentences.zh: 至孝武帝甯康中，遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Xiaowu's Ningkang period, he dispatched envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiaowu's Ningkang era Fo again sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 至義熙中，每歲又來寇日南、九真、九德等諸郡，殺傷甚衆，交州遂致虛弱，而林邑亦用疲弊。

translations.literal: Reaching the Yixi period, each year they again came raiding the commanderies of Rinan, Jiuzhen, Jiude, and others, killing and wounding very many; Jiaozhou thereupon became hollow and weak, while Linyi also became exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Yixi years he raided Rinan, Jiuzhen, and Jiude yearly, bleeding Jiaozhou white while exhausting his own realm.

sentences.zh: 佛死，子胡達立，上疏貢金盤椀及金鉦等物。

translations.literal: When Fo died, his son Huda succeeded and submitted a memorial presenting gold trays, bowls, and gongs and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Fo was succeeded by Huda, who sent gold vessels with his memorial.
