translations.idiomatic: — (source table divider)

sentences.zh: 扶南

translations.literal: Funan.
translations.idiomatic: Funan

sentences.zh: =扶南西去林邑三千餘-{里}-，在海大灣中，其境廣袤三千里，有城邑宮室。

translations.literal: [Table entry:] Funan is more than three thousand li west of Linyi, in a great bay of the sea; its territory extends three thousand li east-west and it has walled towns and palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Funan sits three thousand li west of Linyi in a great gulf, with cities across three thousand li of coast.

sentences.zh: 人皆醜黑拳發，倮身跣行。

translations.literal: People are all ugly, black, with curled hair, naked-bodied and go barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: The people are dark, woolly-haired, and go nearly naked.

sentences.zh: 性質直，不爲寇盜，以耕種爲務，一歲種，三歲獲。

translations.literal: Their nature is simple and straight; they do not act as bandits; they take plowing and planting as their task; they plant one year and harvest the third year.
translations.idiomatic: They are honest farmers who sow one year and reap the third.

sentences.zh: 又好雕文刻鏤，食器多以銀爲之，貢賦以金銀珠香。

translations.literal: They also love carved patterns and inlay; eating vessels are mostly of silver; tribute and tax are in gold, silver, pearls, and incense.
translations.idiomatic: They carve silver tableware and pay tribute in gold, pearls, and incense.

sentences.zh: 亦有書記府庫，文字有類于胡。

translations.literal: They also have writing, records, and treasuries; writing somewhat resembles Hu script.
translations.idiomatic: They keep archives in a script akin to Kharosthi.

sentences.zh: 喪葬婚姻略同林邑。

translations.literal: Funerals, marriage, and mourning broadly resemble Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage and mourning echo Linyi custom.

sentences.zh: 其王本是女子，字葉柳。

translations.literal: Their king was originally a woman, styled Yeliu.
translations.idiomatic: Their first monarch was a woman named Yeliu.

sentences.zh: 時有外國人混潰者，先事神，夢神賜之弓，又教載舶入海。

translations.literal: At that time there was a foreigner Hunhun who first served the spirits; he dreamed the spirits gave him a bow and also taught him to load a ship and enter the sea.
translations.idiomatic: A stranger Hunhun dreamed the gods gave him a bow and bade him sail to Funan.

sentences.zh: 混潰旦詣神祠，得弓，遂隨賈人泛海至扶南外邑。

translations.literal: Hunhun at dawn went to the spirit shrine, obtained the bow, then followed merchants drifting on the sea to an outer town of Funan.
translations.idiomatic: He took the bow at dawn and rode merchant ships to a Funan port.

sentences.zh: 葉柳率衆禦之，混潰舉弓，葉柳懼，遂降之。

translations.literal: Yeliu led the host to resist him; Hunhun raised the bow; Yeliu feared and thereupon submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Queen Yeliu marched against him, quailed when he raised the divine bow, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 於是混潰納以爲妻，而據其國。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hunhun took her as wife and occupied her state.
translations.idiomatic: Hunhun married her and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 後胤衰微，子孫不紹，其將範尋復世王扶南矣。

translations.literal: Later descendants declined and weakened, sons and grandsons did not continue; their general Fan Xun again in generations ruled Funan.
translations.idiomatic: Later kings failed; general Fan Xun restored the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 武帝泰始初，遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's Taishi beginning, he dispatched envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At Taishi's start the king sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 太康中，又頻來。

translations.literal: In the Taikang period, they again came frequently.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang saw repeated embassies.

sentences.zh: 穆帝升平初，復有竺旃檀稱王，遣使貢馴象。

translations.literal: At Emperor Mu's Shengping beginning, again there was Zhu Zhantan who called himself king and dispatched envoys to present a tame elephant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shengping a ruler styled Zhu Zhantan sent a trained elephant.

sentences.zh: 帝以殊方異獸，恐爲人患，詔還之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because it was a strange beast from an alien quarter, feared it would become a people's bane, and ordered it returned.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared a rogue elephant and sent it home.

sentences.zh: 北狄

translations.literal: Northern Di.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Di

sentences.zh: 北狄，匈奴。

translations.literal: Among the Northern Di—the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Di section opens with the Xiongnu.

translations.literal: The line is an equals sign used as a table marker in the transmitted layout.
translations.idiomatic: — (source table divider)

sentences.zh: 匈奴

translations.literal: The Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu

sentences.zh: =匈奴之類，總謂之北狄。

translations.literal: [Table entry:] The kinds of the Xiongnu are collectively called the Northern Di.
translations.idiomatic: All northern steppe peoples are classed as Xiongnu here.

sentences.zh: 匈奴地南接燕趙，北暨沙漠，東連九夷，西距六戎。

translations.literal: Xiongnu land south joins Yan and Zhao, north reaches the desert, east links the nine Yi, west borders the six Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Their steppe runs from Yan-Zhao to the desert, from the eastern Yi to the western Rong.

sentences.zh: 世世自相君臣，不稟中國正朔。

translations.literal: Generation after generation they set up rulers among themselves and do not accept the correct new year of China.
translations.idiomatic: They keep their own calendar and khans, ignoring Chinese reign titles.

sentences.zh: 夏曰薰鬻，殷曰鬼方，周曰獫狁，漢曰匈奴。

translations.literal: In Xia they were called Xunyu; in Yin, Guifang; in Zhou, Xianyun; in Han, Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Xia knew them as Xunyu, Shang as Guifang, Zhou as Xianyun, Han as Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 其強弱盛衰、風俗好尚區域所在，皆列于前史。

translations.literal: Their strength and weakness, rise and decline, customs and preferences, and regional locations are all arrayed in former histories.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories already narrate their waxing, waning, and ways.

sentences.zh: 前漢末，匈奴大亂，五單于爭立，而呼韓邪單于失其國，攜率部落，入臣於漢。

translations.literal: At the end of Former Han the Xiongnu fell into great chaos; five shanyus contended for the throne, and Shanyu Huhanye lost his state, gathered and led tribes, and entered to serve Han.
translations.idiomatic: Late Former Han split the steppe among five shanyus; Huhanye lost and submitted to Han.

sentences.zh: 漢嘉其意，割并州並界以安之。

translations.literal: Han praised his intent and carved out territory bordering Bing Province to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Han rewarded him with pasture along Bingzhou's frontier.

sentences.zh: 於是匈奴五千餘落入居朔方諸郡，與漢人雜處。

translations.literal: Thereupon more than five thousand camps of Xiongnu entered and dwelt in the various commanderies of Shuofang, mixed dwelling with Han people.
translations.idiomatic: Over five thousand Xiongnu camps settled inside Shuofang and mingled with Han farmers.

sentences.zh: 呼韓邪感漢恩，來朝，漢因留之，賜其邸舍，猶因本號，聽稱單于，歲給綿絹錢穀，有如列侯。

translations.literal: Huhanye felt Han kindness, came to court; Han therefore detained him, granted him a mansion, still followed the original title, allowed him to be called shanyu, yearly supplying silks, cash, and grain like a ranked marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Huhanye, grateful for Han favor, stayed at court in a subsidized mansion, kept his shanyu title, and drew a stipend like a Chinese noble.

sentences.zh: 子孫傳襲，歷代不絕。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons transmitted inheritance; generation after generation did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: His line held the title for generations without break.

sentences.zh: 其部落隨所居郡縣，使宰牧之，與編戶大同，而不輸貢賦。

translations.literal: Their tribes followed whatever commandery or county they dwelt in, had magistrates shepherd them, were largely the same as registered households, yet did not render tribute or tax.
translations.idiomatic: They were administered like commoners but paid no taxes.

sentences.zh: 多歷年所，戶口漸滋，彌漫北朔，轉難禁制。

translations.literal: Many years passed; household registrations gradually multiplied, spread across the northern frontier, and became ever harder to restrain.
translations.idiomatic: Their numbers swelled along the northern marches until control frayed.

sentences.zh: 後漢末，天下騷動，群臣競言胡人猥多，懼必爲寇，宜先爲其防。

translations.literal: At the end of Later Han the realm was in turmoil; ministers vied to say the Hu were too many and feared they would surely become bandits—it was fit first to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han ministers panicked that inner Hu settlers would rebel.

sentences.zh: 建安中，魏武帝始分其衆爲五部，部立其中貴者爲帥，選漢人爲司馬以監督之。

translations.literal: In the Jian'an period, Wei Wu Di first divided their masses into five divisions; each division set up one of their nobles as commander and selected Han men as majors to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao split them into five divisions overseen by Han majors.

sentences.zh: 魏末，復改帥爲都尉。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei, again the commanders were changed to commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Wei renamed the tribal commanders as commandants.

sentences.zh: 其左部都尉所統可萬餘落，居於太原故茲氏縣；

translations.literal: What the commandant of the left division commanded was more than ten thousand camps, dwelling in former Zishi county of Taiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: The left commandant led over ten thousand camps around old Zishi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 右部都尉可六千餘落，居祁縣；

translations.literal: the right division commandant, more than six thousand camps, dwelt in Qi county;
translations.idiomatic: The right commandant had six thousand camps in Qi county.

sentences.zh: 南部都尉可三千餘落，居蒲子縣；

translations.literal: the southern division commandant, more than three thousand camps, dwelt in Puzi county;
translations.idiomatic: The southern commandant held three thousand camps at Puzi.

sentences.zh: 北部都尉可四千餘落，居新興縣；

translations.literal: the northern division commandant, more than four thousand camps, dwelt in Xinxing county;
translations.idiomatic: The northern commandant had four thousand camps in Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 中部都尉可六千餘落，居大陵縣。

translations.literal: the central division commandant, more than six thousand camps, dwelt in Daling county.
translations.idiomatic: The central commandant led six thousand camps at Daling.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼後，塞外匈奴大水，塞泥、黑難等二萬餘落歸化，帝復納之，使居河西故宜陽城下。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu ascended the throne, beyond the passes the Xiongnu suffered great flood; Saini, Heinan, and others more than twenty thousand camps submitted to transformation; the emperor again accepted them and made them dwell below the old Yiyang city west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Wudi admitted twenty thousand flood refugees from beyond the wall and parked them west of the Yellow River near old Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 後復與晉人雜居，由是平陽、西河、太原、新興、上党、樂平諸郡靡不有焉。

translations.literal: Afterwards again they mixed dwelt with Jin people; therefore in the commanderies of Pingyang, Xihe, Taiyuan, Xinxing, Shangdang, and Leping there was none without them.
translations.idiomatic: They soon mingled with Jin subjects across Pingyang, Xihe, Taiyuan, Xinxing, Shangdang, and Leping.

sentences.zh: ，單于猛叛，屯孔邪城。

translations.literal: (Continuing,) Shanyu Meng rebelled and encamped at Kongye city.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyu Meng then rebelled from Kongye.

sentences.zh: 武帝遣婁侯何楨持節討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu dispatched Marquis Lou He Zhen bearing the staff of authority to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi sent He Zhen with imperial baton to crush the revolt.

sentences.zh: 楨素有志略，以猛衆凶悍，非少兵所制，乃潛誘猛左部督李恪殺猛，於是匈奴震服，積年不敢復反。

translations.literal: Zhen by nature had strategy; because Meng's host was fierce and hardy and could not be controlled by few troops, he secretly enticed Meng's left-division inspector Li Ke to kill Meng; thereupon the Xiongnu trembled and submitted and for accumulated years dared not rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhen bribed Meng's officer Li Ke to assassinate him, cowing the horde for years.

sentences.zh: 其後稍因忿恨，殺害長史，漸爲邊患。

translations.literal: Afterwards gradually because of resentment they killed chief clerks and step by step became a border calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Later grudges led them to murder Chinese officials and stir frontier trouble.

sentences.zh: 侍御史西河郭欽上疏曰：

translations.literal: Attending censor Guo Qin of Xihe submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Censor Guo Qin of Xihe memorialized the throne:

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored him.

sentences.zh: 至，復有匈奴胡太阿厚率其部落二萬九千三百人歸化。

translations.literal: When he arrived, again there was Xiongnu Hu Tai Ahou who led his tribe twenty-nine thousand three hundred persons to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Later the chieftain Tai Ahou brought twenty-nine thousand followers to surrender.

sentences.zh: 七年，又有匈奴胡都大博及萎莎胡等各率種類大小凡十萬餘口，詣雍州刺史扶風王駿降附。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, again there were Xiongnu Hu Dubo and Weisha Hu and others, each leading their kinds great and small, in all more than one hundred thousand persons, who went to Inspector of Yong Province, Prince Jun of Fufeng, to surrender and attach.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Dubo, Weisha Hu, and others delivered over a hundred thousand people to Prince Sima Jun of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 明年，匈奴都督大豆得一育鞠等復率種落大小萬一千五百口，牛二萬二千頭，羊十萬五千口，車廬什物不可勝紀，來降，並貢其方物，帝並撫納之。

translations.literal: The next year, Xiongnu commandant Doudou Deyi Yuju and others again led camps great and small eleven thousand five hundred persons, oxen twenty-two thousand head, sheep one hundred five thousand head, carts, huts, and goods beyond counting, came to submit, and together presented their local products; the emperor all soothed and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Next year another column brought eleven thousand five hundred families, vast herds, and baggage; the court admitted them all.

sentences.zh: 北狄以部落爲類，其入居塞者有屠各種、鮮支種、寇頭種、烏譚種、赤勒種、捍蛭種、黑狼種、赤沙種、鬱鞞種、萎莎種、禿童種、勃蔑種、羌渠種、賀賴種、鐘跂種、大樓種、雍屈種、真樹種、力羯種，凡十九種，皆有部落，不相雜錯。

translations.literal: The Northern Di classify by tribe; those who entered within the passes include the Tuge branch, Xianzhi branch, Koutou branch, Wutan branch, Chile branch, Hazhi branch, Heilang branch, Chisha branch, Yubi branch, Weisha branch, Tutong branch, Bomie branch, Qiangqu branch, Helai branch, Zhongqi branch, Dalou branch, Yongqu branch, Zhenshu branch, and Lijie branch—nineteen kinds in all—each having tribes and not intermixing wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Xiongnu splintered into nineteen named branches—Tuge, Xianzhi, Koutou, and the rest—each keeping separate camps.

sentences.zh: 屠各最豪貴，故得爲單于，統領諸種。

translations.literal: The Tuge are the most powerful and noble; therefore they can be shanyu and command the various kinds.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuge were highest and supplied the shanyu who ruled the rest.

sentences.zh: 其國號有左賢王、右賢王、左奕蠡王、右奕蠡王、左于陸王、右于陸王、左漸尚王、右漸尚王、左朔方王、右朔方王、左獨鹿王、右獨鹿王、左顯祿王、右顯祿王、左安樂王、右安樂王、凡十六等，皆用單于親子弟也。

translations.literal: Their state titles include Left Worthy King, Right Worthy King, Left Guili King, Right Guili King, Left Yulu King, Right Yulu King, Left Jianshang King, Right Jianshang King, Left Shuofang King, Right Shuofang King, Left Dulu King, Right Dulu King, Left Xianlu King, Right Xianlu King, Left Anle King, Right Anle King—in all sixteen ranks—all are the shanyu's close sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen royal titles—worthy kings, guili kings, and so on—went to the khan's brothers and sons.

sentences.zh: 其左賢王最貴，唯太子得居之。

translations.literal: The Left Worthy King is the most honored; only the heir apparent may occupy it.
translations.idiomatic: Left Worthy King was the highest post, reserved for the heir.

sentences.zh: 其四姓，有呼延氏、卜氏、蘭氏、喬氏。

translations.literal: The four surnames are Huyan, Bu, Lan, and Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Four great clans were Huyan, Bu, Lan, and Qiao.

sentences.zh: 而呼延氏最貴，則有左日逐、右日逐，世爲輔相；

translations.literal: Among them the Huyan are the most noble; then there are Left Rizhu and Right Rizhu, generation after generation serving as ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Huyan chiefs monopolized the Left and Right Rizhu posts as hereditary chancellors.

sentences.zh: 卜氏則有左沮渠、右沮渠；

translations.literal: The Bu then have Left Juqu and Right Juqu.
translations.idiomatic: The Bu clan held Left and Right Juqu offices.

sentences.zh: 蘭氏則有左當戶、右當戶；

translations.literal: The Lan then have Left Danghu and Right Danghu.
translations.idiomatic: The Lan clan held Left and Right Danghu.

sentences.zh: 喬氏則有左都侯、右都侯。

translations.literal: The Qiao then have Left Douhou and Right Douhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiao clan held Left and Right Douhou.

sentences.zh: 又有車陽、沮渠、餘地諸雜號，猶中國百官也。

translations.literal: Further there are miscellaneous titles such as Cheyang, Juqu, Yudi—like the hundred officials of China.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous titles mirrored Chinese bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 其國人有綦毋氏、勒氏、皆勇健，好反叛。

translations.literal: Among their countrymen there are the Qiwu and Le clans—both brave and hardy, fond of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Qiwu and Le families were famed warriors and rebels.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，有騎督綦毋伣邪伐吳有功，遷赤沙都尉。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's time there was Cavalry Inspector Qiwu Xianye who attacked Wu with merit and was promoted to Chisha commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi promoted Qiwu Xianye, who had served against Wu, to commandant of Chisha.

sentences.zh: 惠帝元康中，匈奴郝散攻上黨，殺長吏，入守上郡。

translations.literal: In Emperor Hui's Yuankang period, Xiongnu Hao San attacked Shangdang, killed senior clerks, and entered to hold Shang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang saw Hao San seize Shangdang and kill its officials.

sentences.zh: 明年，散弟度元又率馮翊、北地羌胡攻破二郡。

translations.literal: The next year, San's younger brother Duyuan again led Fengyi and Beidi Qiang and Hu and broke the two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Duyuan then smashed Fengyi and Beidi with Qiang and Hu allies.

sentences.zh: 自此已後，北狄漸盛，中原亂矣。

translations.literal: From this onward the Northern Di gradually grew strong and the Central Plain fell into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: After that the northern tribes grew bold and China slid into chaos.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historiographers' judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Historiographers' appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫宵形稟氣，是稱萬物之靈，系土隨方，乃有群分之異。

translations.literal: The court historians say: Bearing form and receiving breath is called the spirit of the myriad things; tethered to soil and following region, then there are differences of the many divisions.
translations.idiomatic: They write: endowed with form and breath, humankind is cleverest, yet geography divides barbarian from Chinese.

sentences.zh: 蹈仁義者爲中寓，肆凶獷者爲外夷，譬諸草木，區以別矣。

translations.literal: Those who tread benevolence and righteousness are the inner dwellers; those who unleash fierce brutality are the outer Yi; likened to plants and trees, they are separated by zones.
translations.idiomatic: The humane belong to the heartland; the savage dwell beyond—like plants sorted by soil.

sentences.zh: 夷狄之徒，名教所絕，窺邊侯隙，自古爲患，稽諸前史，憑陵匪一。

translations.literal: The tribes of the Yi and Di lie outside name-teaching; spying on the border and waiting for gaps has been a calamity since antiquity; checking former histories, their arrogance is not one case.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier peoples stand outside Confucian rites and have raided whenever China weakened.

sentences.zh: 軒皇北逐，唐帝南征，殷後東戡，周王西狩，皆所以禦其侵亂也。

translations.literal: The August Xuan drove them north; the Tang emperor campaigned south; the Yin successor chastised east; the Zhou king hunted west—all to ward off their invasions.
translations.idiomatic: Sage-kings struck in every direction to repel them.

sentences.zh: 嬴劉之際，匈奴最強；

translations.literal: Between the First Emperor and Liu Bang, the Xiongnu were strongest;
translations.idiomatic: Between Qin Shihuang and Gaozu the Xiongnu peaked;

sentences.zh: 元成之間，呼韓委質，漢嘉其節，處之中壤。

translations.literal: between Yuandi and Chengdi, Huhanye offered his person; Han praised his integrity and settled him in the central soil.
translations.idiomatic: under Yuandi and Chengdi Huhanye submitted and Han lodged him inside the wall.

sentences.zh: 歷年斯永，種類逾繁，舛號殊名，不可勝載。

translations.literal: Years stretched long; kinds multiplied beyond measure; contrary titles and different names cannot all be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Centuries passed, clans multiplied, and titles beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 爰及泰始，匪革前迷，廣辟塞垣，更招種落，納萎莎之後附，開育鞠之新降，接帳連韝，充郊掩甸。

translations.literal: Down to Taishi they did not reform the former error; they widened the frontier palisades and again summoned tribes, accepting Weisha followers and opening new submissions like Yuju, tent lines touching bridles, filling the suburbs and covering the meadows.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi widened the frontier, welcomed Weisha and Yuju bands until camps carpeted the inner pasture.

sentences.zh: 既而沸脣成俗，鳴鏑爲群，振鴞響而挻災，恣狼心而逞暴。

translations.literal: Thereupon frothing lips became custom, whistling arrows formed packs; they roused owl cries to spread disaster and indulged wolf hearts to display cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: They grew arrogant, rode in war bands, and turned wolfish.

sentences.zh: 何楨縱策，弗沮於奸萌；

translations.literal: He Zhen deployed stratagems yet could not stop the sprouts of treason;
translations.idiomatic: Even He Zhen's plots could not choke the conspiracy at birth;

sentences.zh: 郭欽馳疏，無救於妖漸。

translations.literal: Guo Qin's flying memorial could not save the gradual rise of portents.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qin's urgent memorial could not halt the gathering storm.

sentences.zh: 未環星紀，坐傾都邑，黎元塗地，凶族滔天。

translations.literal: Before a full cycle of stars, sitting, they overturned the capital; common folk were smeared on the ground and the vicious kindred flooded heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Within a dozen years they overturned Luoyang and drowned the realm in blood.

sentences.zh: 跡其所由，抑武皇之失也。

translations.literal: Tracing how it arose, perhaps it was Emperor Wu's fault.
translations.idiomatic: The editors blame this on Emperor Wu's policy.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾分緒偽燕，遠辭正嫡，率東胡之餘衆，掩西羌之舊宇，綱疏政暇，地廣兵全，廓萬里之基，貽一匡之訓，弗忘忠義，良可嘉焉。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun split off from false Yan, departed far from the true heir, led the remnant hosts of the eastern Hu, and covered the old territory of the western Qiang; nets were loose and government leisurely, the land was broad and arms intact—he laid a foundation of ten thousand li and handed down a lesson of restoration; not forgetting loyalty and righteousness is truly praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun broke from Murong Yan, led Donghu remnants west, seized Qiang grazing lands, built a vast realm, and kept faith with Jin—worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 吐延夙標宏偉，見方于項籍，始遵朝化，遽夭于姜聰，高節不群，亦殊籓之秀也。

translations.literal: Tuyan early displayed greatness and was compared to Xiang Yu; he first followed court transformation yet suddenly perished at Jiang Cong's hand—high integrity, not herd-like, is also excellence among distant vassals.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyan, likened to Xiang Yu, died serving Jin against a Qiang blade—a frontier hero.

sentences.zh: 葉延至孝，寄新哀於射草；

translations.literal: Yeyan was utmost filial, lodging fresh grief in shooting straw;
translations.idiomatic: Yeyan vented grief on straw effigies—paragon filial piety;

sentences.zh: 辟奚深友，邁古烈于分荊；

translations.literal: Pixi was deep in friendship, surpassing ancient fierceness in splitting thorns;
translations.idiomatic: Pixi loved brothers beyond the call—rare loyalty;

sentences.zh: 視連蒸蒸，光奉先之義；

translations.literal: Shilian was diligent, brightening the duty of serving ancestors;
translations.idiomatic: Shilian honored his father's memory;

sentences.zh: 視羆矯矯，蘊經時之略；

translations.literal: Shirong was proud and tall, hoarding stratagems for the age;
translations.idiomatic: Shirong harbored grand strategy;

sentences.zh: 洛幹童幼，早擅英規，未騁雄心，先摧凶手，奉順者必敗，豈天亡晉乎！

translations.literal: Shuluogan in childhood early grasped heroic plans; before his great heart could gallop, he first was broken by a villain's hand—those who obeyed the way were sure to fail: was it Heaven that destroyed Jin?
translations.idiomatic: Boy-king Shuluogan showed genius yet fell to treachery—almost as if heaven had doomed Jin.

sentences.zh: 且渾廆連枝，生自邊極，各謀孫而翼子，咸革裔而希華。

translations.literal: Moreover Hun and Hui were branches of one tree, born on the farthest border, each plotting for grandsons and sons, all altering seed and hoping to become Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: Hun and Hui were brothers from the edge of the world, yet one line turned Chinese while the other stayed steppe.

sentences.zh: 廆胤奸凶，假鳳圖而竊號，渾嗣忠謹，距龍涸而歸誠。

translations.literal: Hui's descendants were treacherous and fierce, borrowing phoenix auguries to usurp titles; Hun's heirs stayed loyal and careful, refusing Longqi and returning sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui's line seized the Yan throne; Tuyuhun's line kept faith with western Jin.

sentences.zh: 懷奸者數世而亡，資忠者累葉彌劭，積善余慶，斯言信矣。

translations.literal: Those who harbored treachery perished in a few generations; those who relied on loyalty grew stronger age after age—'good deeds leave blessings'—this saying is trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Treachery burned out fast; loyalty flourished—proving the proverb that virtue brings reward.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：逖矣前王，區別群方。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Far indeed the former kings, who distinguished the many regions.
translations.idiomatic: Verse: ancient kings drew borders among the peoples.

sentences.zh: 叛由德弛，朝因化昌。

translations.literal: Rebellion came when virtue slackened; court flourished when transformation prospered.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion followed lost virtue; order followed true teaching.

sentences.zh: 武后升圖，智昧遷胡。

translations.literal: The heirs of the martial emperor ascended the throne-chart; wisdom was dim regarding relocating the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's successors took the throne with little wit for the Hu settlers they had invited inside.

sentences.zh: 遽淪家國，多謝明謨。

translations.literal: Suddenly state and family sank—much thanks to those wise plans.
translations.idiomatic: Throne and hearth were lost—little thanks to the court's vaunted wisdom.

sentences.zh: 谷渾英奮，思矯穨運；

translations.literal: Tuyuhun rose heroically, intending to correct the fallen fortune;
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun strove to mend the broken age;

sentences.zh: 克昌其緒，實資忠訓。

translations.literal: to make his line flourish truly relied on loyal instruction.
translations.idiomatic: and his house endured through loyal teaching.
